evaluation_notes: Requirements S1-S13 (requirements_analysis.json) are the primary criteria; quality attributes (quality_attributes.json) and drivers (drivers.json) complement them.

Requirement and driver status scale: satisfied | partially_satisfied | not_satisfied | unclear. A requirement-level inconsistency (e.g. S2 30 min vs 30 s, S6 90 min vs S10) does not by itself lower the status when the alternative supports either reading; it is recorded in the rationale.
Quality-attribute impact scale: positive | slightly_positive | neutral | mixed | slightly_negative | negative. Impact is judged against the attribute description in quality_attributes.json.

Evidence cites alternatives.json (description, key_decisions, compatibility_conditions_applied, assumptions, limitations) and pattern_candidates.json where a selected pattern's documented scope is used.
Where satisfaction depends on an assumption stated by the alternative, the assumption is named; satisfaction is not assumed where the alternative does not allocate the responsibility.
No trade-off analysis, ranking or recommendation is performed here.

requirement_evaluations.rationale: Registration is allocated to the Identity & Access module and personal data is stored in a segregated, encrypted schema accessible only to that module. 'End-to-end encryption between user device and app database' is only met under the alternative's own reading (TLS on all hops plus encryption at rest), which it marks as unconfirmed; no provision is made for the strict reading (data unreadable by intermediate layers).

alternatives.json A1.assumptions: ''End-to-end encryption' (S1) is satisfied by TLS on all hops plus encryption at rest of sensitive data; this reading is unconfirmed.'
requirements_analysis.json S1.ambiguities: E2E encryption meaning unclear

requirement_evaluations.rationale: A Notification & Verification module sends codes through SMS/email adapters protected by timeouts/retries/circuit breakers; the selected Scheduler / Durable Timer pattern covers verification-code expiry. Either validity period (30 min or 30 s) can be configured; the inconsistency is a requirement issue.
